title: Financial stocks hold Nifty steady at midday; Auto, FMCG drag - The HinduBusinessLine
text:
Benchmark indices were nearly flat at midday on Thursday, with financial stocks providing support even as automobiles and consumer goods weighed on sentiment. The BSE Sensex was trading at 81,930.41, up 51.01 points or 0.06 per cent, while the NSE Nifty 50 was at 25,255.55, up just 0.50 points or 0.00 per cent, as of 12.50 pm, marking the first session since October 9 where the index stayed within the range of the previous bar.

Insurance and financial stocks dominated the gainers board on the Nifty 50. HDFC Life Insurance surged 3.91 per cent to ₹596.00, the top gainer, followed by Shriram Finance, which crossed the ₹1,000 mark to trade at ₹1,003.15, up 3.51 per cent. Bajaj Finance rose 3.06 per cent to ₹1,111.80, SBI Life Insurance gained 2.61 per cent to ₹1,813.20, and Bajaj Finserv added 2.27 per cent to ₹1,886.90.

On the losing side, Mahindra & Mahindra was the biggest drag, falling 2.51 per cent to ₹3,378.00. Nestlé India declined 2.11 per cent to ₹1,260.80, Maruti Suzuki slid 1.84 per cent to ₹12,942.00, and Hindustan Unilever dropped 1.44 per cent to ₹1,974.50. TMPV fell 1.42 per cent to ₹295.00. The auto and FMCG sectors remained under broad pressure through the morning session.

Among sectoral indices, Nifty Realty was the best performer, while Nifty IT was the worst. Bank Nifty continued to outperform, with HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank, and SBI as the top contributors to its gains. Market breadth on the BSE was positive, with 2,441 stocks advancing against 1,794 declining, while 262 remained unchanged. A total of 127 stocks hit fresh 52-week highs versus 39 at 52-week lows.

SBI Securities noted that resistance for the Nifty lies in the zone of 25,430–25,450, with support at 25,120–25,140. .....”In an event of a surge above 25,450, the index can experience an extension of the rally towards 25,600,”... the firm said, while adding that a slip below 25,120 would shift focus to the next support band of 24,950–24,970. On the options front, meaningful call writing was seen at the 25,300 and 25,400 strikes, with substantial put open interest at the 25,200 strike. The Nifty’s advance-decline ratio stood at 22:28. For the Sensex, support is pegged at 81,600 and resistance at 82,500.

Ponmudi R, CEO of Enrich Money, observed that markets staged an early recovery after a subdued open: ...”Banking and financial stocks led the rebound, providing the primary support to the market, although gains remained uneven across sectors, pointing to a degree of caution in broader market participation.”...

In commodities, MCX crude oil fell sharply, trading near ₹8,050 per barrel, down about 1.6 per cent, weighed by a stronger US dollar even as geopolitical uncertainty around Iran’s nuclear programme provided some support. WTI crude was near $85.75, down about 0.8 per cent. ...”Iran’s security chief said Tehran will not allow any enriched nuclear material to leave the country, while Washington says nuclear matters must be part of any initial talks,”... according to Enrich Money’s market update, keeping a risk premium in oil prices despite the broader decline.

Gold came under fresh pressure as the dollar index climbed toward its highest level since April 2025. MCX December gold was trading near ₹1,39,230 per 10 grams, down about 0.3 per cent, while COMEX gold was near $3,985 per ounce, extending a three-session decline below the key $4,000 level. MCX silver was near ₹1,83,200 per kg, down about 0.7 per cent, with COMEX silver at $51.45, down about 1 per cent. ...”A firmer dollar and US 10-year yields pressing against 5 per cent are weighing on the whole precious complex,”... the Enrich Money update noted, adding that markets are now fully pricing in a 25 basis point Federal Reserve rate hike in December, with bets on a 50 basis point move rising to around 13 per cent.

The rupee was trading near 93.77 against the US dollar, up about 0.1 per cent on the day. BSE-listed companies carried a combined market capitalisation of ₹5,12,16,160.93 crore, equivalent to $5.46 trillion. The October CPI inflation print, due later in the day, remains the key domestic trigger, with elevated readings potentially reinforcing the case for further Reserve Bank of India tightening.
